Abuse Case: An unauthorized person may impersonate a legitimate user or service identity.
Mitigation: Use unique test accounts, strong authentication, MFA where supported, and secure session handling.

Abuse Case: An attacker may alter application input or stored records without authorization.
Mitigation: Validate input server-side; enforce authorization on every change; use parameterized queries and integrity checks.

Abuse Case: A user may deny an action if security-relevant events are not logged.
Mitigation: Record timestamped security events with actor and outcome; protect logs from alteration; avoid logging secrets.

Abuse Case: Sensitive training data, configuration, or credentials may be exposed.
Mitigation: Minimize data, enforce least privilege, encrypt sensitive data, redact logs, and restrict evidence access.

Abuse Case: Excessive requests or resource exhaustion may disrupt service.
Mitigation: Use rate limiting, resource monitoring, safe request limits, and operational alerts. Do not perform DoS tests.

Abuse Case: A low-privilege account may gain permissions beyond its intended role.
Mitigation: Apply server-side role-based access control, least privilege, and authorization checks on sensitive actions.
